chunks: Muhammad ibn Yahya, from Muhammad ibn Ahmad, from al-Hasan ibn Musa, from Ghiyath ibn Kaloub, from Is'haq ibn 'Ammar, from Ja'far, from his forefathers (peace be upon them)
That Ali (peace be upon him) disliked the Hajj and Umrah to be performed upon the camels feeding on dung.

key_terms.يَكْرَهُ: Disliked (a juristic term indicating dislike but not necessarily prohibition)

ai.seo_question: What is the ruling on performing Hajj on dung-feeding camels?
ai.summary: Imam Ali (peace be upon him) disliked performing Hajj and Umrah on 'jalalat' camels—those feeding on dung—emphasizing that ritual excellence extends to the physical purity of the mount used for worship. This narration, found in al-Kafi, reflects the Shia scholarly emphasis on removing both physical and spiritual impurities (najāsah) from the components of ibadah, ensuring the act is performed with dignity and cleanliness.
